clue.text: Look down on people initially invading Middle East

indicators.note: the initial letters are said to invade, so they go inside the abbreviation for the region
initially asks for only the opening letters of the words on and people

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the people who first poured into the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: To look down can mean to be glum and listless, which is to sulk or brood.

clue.text: Wife not convinced, dismissing a Republican critic

parts.note: in Cockney slang 'my old Dutch' (from duchess of Fife) is one's wife

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so these letters are removed from the word

parts.note: someone not convinced is unclear about the matter

explanation.surface: A doubting wife throws out a Republican commentator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' removes A and R from UNCLEAR, leaving UNCLE. 'Dutch' for a wife is Cockney rhyming slang (duchess of Fife), common in British crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch uncle is someone who gives stern, frank criticism or advice, so it names a kind of critic.

clue.text: Travelling people will scoff, given the chance to move here

definitions.text: Travelling people will scoff, given the chance to move here

parts.words: Travelling people will scoff, given the chance to move here
parts.note: the surface suggests nomads mocking a chance to settle, but it describes the railway carriage where passengers on a journey move along to eat

explanation.surface: Nomads sneer at an offer to come and settle in one place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling people' are train passengers, 'scoff' means eat greedily, and 'move here' means walk along the train to this carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage serving meals is where travellers go to eat during a journey.

clue.text: Composer right to avoid scornful comments

indicators.note: the letter is made to avoid the word, so it is taken out

parts.note: satire is mocking, scornful commentary

explanation.surface: A composer stays correct by steering clear of mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid' drops R from SATIRE. Erik Satie was a French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, best known for his Gymnopédies.

clue.text: Reformer will enthral one craftsman in the music business

indicators.note: to enthral is literally to hold captive, so the reformer's name holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: Martin Luther led the Protestant Reformation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A reformer will captivate a single instrument-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A luthier makes stringed instruments such as violins and guitars, a craft serving music.

clue.text: President ignoring note about a shocking event

indicators.note: the shortened name goes about the letter, enclosing it
ignoring means leaving out, so the letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Harry Truman was a US president

explanation.surface: A president disregards a memo about some shocking incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops N from TRUMAN to give TRUMA, and 'about' puts A inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a deeply distressing experience or shock.

clue.text: What Moriarty well knew would upset Holmes, mostly re ambition

indicators.note: upset means overturned and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter of the detective's name is used

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sherlock's nemesis knows something that would unsettle Holmes's aims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims HOLMES to HOLME; with RE and AMBITION, 'upset' rearranges them. In Conan Doyle, Professor Moriarty wrote a treatise on the binomial theorem.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes says Professor Moriarty wrote a celebrated treatise on this mathematical result, so it is something he knew well.

clue.text: Trivial old female caught interfering in twelve series

indicators.note: the letter interferes by getting into the middle of the word for midday

parts.note: twelve o'clock is noon
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a series is a sequence

explanation.surface: An old woman was caught meddling in a twelve-part serial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interfering in' puts C inside NOON to make NOCON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no consequence is unimportant, which is what trivial means.

clue.text: View a faction seizing power

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the group's word holds the letter inside

parts.note: a sect is a faction or splinter group

explanation.surface: Observing a breakaway group as it grabs control.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is a view, as of a house facing a direction, or an angle on something.

clue.text: Expects everything to be supplied in watering-holes — nothing omitted

indicators.note: the total is supplied in, placed into the middle of the shortened watering-holes
omitted means left out, so the zero letter is dropped

parts.note: oases are watering-holes in the desert
nothing is zero, the letter O
the sum is the whole amount, everything

explanation.surface: Someone presumes all will be laid on in the pubs, with nothing left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitted' drops O from OASES to leave ASES, and 'to be supplied in' puts SUM inside it. Watering-holes suggests pubs but means oases.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume something is to take it as given, to expect or suppose it.

clue.text: Good hotel accommodation for expectant honeymooner?

parts.note: a hotel's accommodation is a room

explanation.surface: Fine hotel lodging booked for newlyweds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because a bridegroom about to go on honeymoon is looking forward to it; the question mark marks the playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom, about to begin married life, is a honeymooner full of anticipation.

clue.text: Poor playing seen around new sport

indicators.note: the two outer pieces are seen around the middle one, enclosing it

parts.note: poor means bad
a show that is playing is on
in mint condition means brand new

explanation.surface: Bad play shown around a fresh game.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Climate change term about to appear in information given to parliament

indicators.note: the short word is to appear in, so it goes inside the word for information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
RE is Latin-derived for about or concerning
a house is a chamber of parliament

explanation.surface: A climate-change expression is about to feature in a briefing to parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear in' puts RE inside GEN to make GREEN. 'Gen' is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: The greenhouse effect, trapping of heat by gases, is a central phrase in talk of global warming.

clue.text: Atmosphere left following charge

indicators.note: following means the abbreviation comes after the payment word

parts.note: a charge is a fee

explanation.surface: Mood abandoned after a fee is levied.
explanation.definitionFit: The feel of a place is its atmosphere or ambience.

clue.text: Centre of stalls is home to bishop without elevated tastes

indicators.note: is home to means houses, so the seat row takes the letter inside

parts.note: in a theatre's stalls the central line of seats is the middle row
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: The middle seats of the theatre stalls house a bishop with lowbrow taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is home to' puts B inside MIDDLE ROW. 'Centre of stalls' looks like a letter pick but means a row of theatre seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlebrow culture is moderately intellectual, lacking highbrow or refined tastes.

clue.text: Grape variety? Zero contained in beer

indicators.note: contained in means the letter sits inside the drink's word

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Wine varieties? No: a pint of beer, with none of anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a family of grapes, such as Pinot Noir and Pinot Grigio.

clue.text: Salad of tuna and rice not initially dubious

indicators.note: a salad is a mixture, so these letters are tossed together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word not is used

explanation.surface: A tuna and rice salad, not at first appealing, is a doubtful dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To be uncertain is to be doubtful, the same as dubious.

clue.text: Article in truck displays weight

indicators.note: in means the article goes inside the vehicle's word

parts.note: a cart is a truck or wagon
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news article in the lorry shows how heavy it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is a unit of weight for gemstones, 200 milligrams.

clue.text: University servant carrying stone away from the audience

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the servant's word holds the weight abbreviation

parts.note: a page is a young servant
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A college attendant carries a rock off out of sight of the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts ST inside PAGE. A stone is a British unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstage is the back of the stage, the part farthest from the audience.

clue.text: Vessel seen in amount of film about a SW river

indicators.note: the can goes about the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a can is a reel's worth of film, as in 'in the can'
the Tamar is a river in south-west England, between Devon and Cornwall

explanation.surface: A boat appears in a can of film about some river in the south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TAMAR and A inside CAN. The Tamar divides Devon and Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a boat with two parallel hulls.

clue.text: Utopian vision at the heart of determined endeavours

indicators.note: at the heart of means the letters lie in the middle of the phrase, spanning its two words

explanation.surface: A dream of paradise lies at the core of resolute efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the archetype of paradise, an ideal place.

clue.text: Unfit though being hired by company?

parts.note: someone hired by an employer is in with them, employed there
a firm is a company

explanation.surface: Not fit for the job, despite being taken on by the business.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'in firm', someone employed by a company; the question mark flags the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means weak or in poor health, physically unfit.

clue.text: Operation of male prison lacking the individual touch

indicators.note: an operation works on something, here working the letters into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Running a men's jail is a cold, faceless business.
explanation.definitionFit: Impersonal means without personal feeling or human warmth.

clue.text: Squares with company about board's highest return

parts.note: nine is a square number, so nines are squares
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Squares in a company discuss the board's best return.
explanation.walkthrough: In darts, the maximum with three darts is three treble twenties, nine twenties or 180, so the dartboard's highest return is nine score.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine score is 180, the top total possible with three darts on a dartboard.

clue.text: Fellow surrounded by the debris mostly opposing groups

indicators.note: surrounded by means the man's word sits inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: debris is dust
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man is trapped amid most of the rubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts DUST to DUS, and 'surrounded by' places MAN inside THE DUS.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Them and us' describes two sides divided against each other, such as bosses and workers.

clue.text: Sailors heading for marina in Northern town end in Whitehaven

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the town's name

parts.note: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, in northern England

indicators.note: heading for gives the head, the opening letter, of the word marina
end in takes the final letter of the place name

explanation.surface: Sailors head to a marina in a northern town and finish in Whitehaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside CREWE, a railway town in Cheshire, north-west England; 'end in' adds the N of Whitehaven, a Cumbrian port.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewmen are members of a ship's crew, so sailors.

clue.text: Funding from many countries perhaps still not in account?

parts.note: the UN is a body of many countries; with 's it is the UN's
aid is funding given to those in need

explanation.surface: International funding perhaps has still not appeared in the accounts?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as UN'S AID, the United Nations' aid. The definition puns on 'account' as a narrative: what is unsaid is left out of any telling.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsaid means not spoken, left out of what anyone recounts.

clue.text: Cheers critical comment? That's not acceptable

parts.note: ta and cheers are both British ways of saying thank you
boo is a jeer, a critical comment

explanation.surface: Thanks, followed by a jeer: that's out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is socially forbidden, beyond what is acceptable.

clue.text: What involves stress encountered by soldiers

parts.note: met means encountered
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps of soldiers

explanation.surface: What causes stress when meeting troops?
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' looks emotional but refers to the emphasis on syllables in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Metre in poetry is the pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables.

clue.text: Curious game played on board set in silver

indicators.note: set in means the game's name is placed inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
go is an East Asian board game

explanation.surface: An inquisitive board game is mounted in silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eager to know, full of curiosity.
